problem: Understanding the computational complexity of verifying properties of ReLU neural networks, such as positivity and function bounds, remains challenging and poorly understood.
approach: The paper proves parameterized hardness results by showing that deciding positivity of 2-layer ReLU networks is W[1]-hard when parameterized by input dimension, and establishes similar hardness for zonotope containment and Lipschitz constant computation.
contribution: Resolves open problems from COLT '25 by proving that network verification problems are W[1]-hard and NP-hard, establishing that naive enumeration methods are essentially optimal under the Exponential Time Hypothesis.

problem: PATE framework struggles with diverse generative tasks like text generation where teacher disagreement increases with output diversity, forcing a tradeoff between diversity and privacy-utility performance.
approach: Hot PATE introduces a diversity-preserving ensemble sampler that uses optimal transport to transfer diversity without incurring additional privacy cost, requiring only API access to proprietary models.
contribution: Shows significant improvements in privacy-utility tradeoff on in-context learning tasks by preserving output diversity while maintaining privacy guarantees.

problem: 3D part segmentation suffers from taxonomy constraints and limited generalization to unseen objects when relying on 2D foundation models that fail to capture intrinsic 3D geometry.
approach: PartSAM employs a triplane-based dual-branch encoder trained natively on large-scale 3D data with over five million shape-part pairs, enabling promptable segmentation of both surface and internal structures.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks with emergent open-world capabilities, enabling accurate part identification and automatic decomposition of 3D shapes.

problem: Layout-to-image generation suffers from attribute leakage due to entangled instance features and poor generalization to novel scenes due to insufficient paired training data.
approach: I-DRUID uses instance-disentanglement modules to extract clean instance representations and applies reinforcement learning with unpaired data to improve generalization to novel scenes.
contribution: Demonstrates improved layout-to-image generation accuracy by combining instance disentanglement with RL on unpaired, prompt-only data to avoid the need for paired data collection.

problem: Computer use agents lack large-scale, open-source training data spanning multiple platforms and domains, limiting progress toward general-purpose GUI automation.
approach: ScaleCUA provides a large-scale dataset across 6 operating systems and 3 task domains built via a closed-loop pipeline combining automated agents with human experts.
contribution: Sets new state-of-the-art results with 94.4% on MMBench-GUI L1-Hard, 60.6% on OSWorld-G, and 47.4% on WebArena-Lite-v2, demonstrating data-driven scaling for computer use agents.

problem: Private domain discovery requires selecting informative subsets of items from unknown domains while preserving differential privacy, a challenging problem under privacy constraints.
approach: Uses the Weighted Gaussian Mechanism as a domain-discovery precursor for top-k and k-hitting set algorithms, providing near-optimal missing mass guarantees on Zipfian data.
contribution: Extends known-domain algorithms to unknown-domain variants with new utility guarantees, demonstrating competitive or superior performance on all three problem types.

problem: Large language models suffer from substantial size that presents deployment and inference challenges, requiring practical compression methods that preserve model abilities.
approach: GPTailor compresses models by strategically merging layers from different finetuned variants through layer removal, selection, and merging operations, posed as a zero-order optimization problem.
contribution: For Llama2-13B, maintains approximately 97.3% of original performance while removing ~25% of parameters, significantly outperforming previous state-of-the-art pruning methods.

problem: Graph retrieval-augmented generation requires joint optimization of graph construction and retrieval, but prior work addresses these in isolation, leading to suboptimal performance especially under domain shift.
approach: Youtu-GraphRAG integrates graph construction, community detection, and retrieval into a unified agentic framework with seed schema guidance and hierarchical knowledge organization.
contribution: Demonstrates robustness across six challenging benchmarks by jointly connecting graph construction with schema-aware extraction and dually-perceived community detection.

problem: Building agentic multimodal models that reliably invoke external tools remains challenging, as direct reinforcement learning alone fails to establish robust tool-use behavior.
approach: DeepEyesV2 uses a two-stage training pipeline: cold-start stage to establish tool-use patterns followed by reinforcement learning to refine tool invocation on diverse, moderately challenging datasets.
contribution: Enables task-adaptive tool invocation with reliable tool integration, demonstrating that systematic tool integration enables complex reasoning across understanding, mathematical, and search-intensive tasks.

problem: Sign-SGD requires manual stepsize selection based on unknown, problem-specific quantities, creating a practical limitation for training large language models.
approach: Parameter-free Sign-SGD removes manual stepsize selection through adaptive methods that work across deterministic, stochastic, and multi-node settings, including momentum variants.
contribution: Matches performance of tuned Sign-SGD and AdamW on LLaMA (130M, 350M) and Swin Transformer (28M) while avoiding tuning overhead and achieving approximately 1.5× end-to-end speedup.

problem: LLM-based planners generate inaccurate plans due to gaps between general knowledge and environment-specific requirements, with iterative refinement incurring substantial query costs.
approach: CoPiC generates diverse high-level planning programs that iteratively produce candidate plans, which a trained domain-adaptive selector evaluates and selects based on alignment with long-term rewards.
contribution: Achieves 19.14% improvement in success rate and 79.39% reduction in token costs on ALFWorld, NetHack, and StarCraft II compared to advanced LLM-based baselines.

problem: Existing world model benchmarks use open-loop protocols that emphasize visual quality in isolation, leaving unclear whether world models actually help agents succeed at embodied tasks.
approach: WoW! benchmarks world models in closed-loop settings that mirror real agent-environment interactions with unified planning strategy, standardized action API, and four diverse environments.
contribution: Reveals that visual quality alone does not guarantee task success (controllability matters more), scaling post-training data is more effective than upgrading pretrained video generators, and more compute improves performance.

problem: Riemannian zeroth-order optimization struggles in geodesically incomplete settings where stationary points may not exist under the original metric.
approach: Constructs structure-preserving metrics that are geodesically complete while ensuring stationary points remain stationary, combining this with intrinsic analysis of zeroth-order estimators.
contribution: Establishes convergence guarantees for SGD matching best-known complexity in geodesically complete settings, with empirical validation on mesh optimization tasks.

problem: MLLM-based image quality assessment primarily relies on general contextual descriptions, limiting fine-grained quality perception of local image regions.
approach: Introduces grounding-IQA paradigm that integrates multimodal referring and grounding with IQA, comprising grounding-IQA-description (with bounding boxes) and visual question answering for local regions.
contribution: Constructs GIQA-160K dataset via automated annotation and develops GIQA-Bench benchmark, demonstrating that fine-grained grounding enables more detailed quality assessment.

problem: Implicit neural representations suffer from spectral bias, limited noise robustness, and difficulty capturing both local and global features despite strong performance across vision tasks.
approach: COSMO-INR leverages harmonic analysis and Chebyshev Polynomials to design activation functions modulated by complex sinusoidal terms that provide complete spectral support throughout the network.
contribution: Provides theoretical proof of improved spectral support through harmonic analysis, develops new activation functions with regularized deep priors, and demonstrates improved INR performance.

problem: Agentic RAG approaches treat retrieval as a black-box querying operation, confining agents to query issuing and hindering their ability to tackle complex information-seeking tasks.
approach: Interact-RAG introduces a Corpus Interaction Engine with action primitives for fine-grained control, enabling agents to manipulate the retrieval process directly through reasoning-enhanced workflow and autonomous end-to-end learning.
contribution: Significantly outperforms advanced methods across six benchmarks by enabling agents to interact with the corpus rather than passively query it.

problem: KV-cache memory footprint scales linearly with sequence length, creating bottlenecks on constrained hardware during long-sequence generation tasks like multi-turn dialogue and chain-of-thought reasoning.
approach: IceCache integrates semantic token clustering with PagedAttention to organize tokens hierarchically and improve cache hit rates, maintaining only the most semantically relevant tokens on GPU.
contribution: Achieves over 99% accuracy with 256-token budget and 97% accuracy with 64-token budget, while using only 25% of full KV-cache token budget on long-sequence scenarios.

problem: Spoken language understanding requires integrating semantic, paralinguistic, and phonological characteristics, but existing benchmarks lack comprehensive linguistic grounding and fine-grained perception evaluation.
approach: MMSU introduces a comprehensive benchmark with 5,000 audio-QA triplets across 47 tasks grounded in linguistic theory, covering phonetics, prosody, rhetoric, syntactics, semantics, and paralinguistics.
contribution: Evaluates 22 advanced SpeechLLMs revealing substantial room for improvement, establishing new standards for comprehensive speech language understanding assessment.

problem: LLM-based multi-agent systems are vulnerable to collective cognitive biases like the Mandela effect, where groups collectively misremember events due to false details and social influence.
approach: Proposes ManBench benchmark with four task types and five interaction protocols to evaluate Mandela effect in multi-agent systems, testing both prompt-level defenses and model-level alignment-based mitigation.
contribution: Demonstrates 74.40% average reduction in Mandela effect through cognitive anchoring, source scrutiny, and alignment-based defenses on the proposed benchmark.

problem: Micro-expression recognition suffers from reliance on pixel-level motion descriptors lacking identity-invariance and domain generalization, combined with scarce annotated data.
approach: D-FACE uses a pretrained facial action tokenizer to shift from pixel-level descriptors to semantic-level facial action tokens, employing Transformer with emotion-description-guided CLIP alignment.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art recognition accuracy with high-quality cross-identity and cross-domain micro-expression generation, demonstrating the paradigm shift from pixel-level to semantic-level representations.

problem: Whether LLM agents can shape co-players' learning dynamics in multi-agent settings remains unexplored, unlike well-studied opponent shaping in reinforcement learning.
approach: ShapeLLM adapts model-free opponent shaping methods for transformer-based agents, enabling LLM agents to influence co-players' behavior in diverse game-theoretic environments.
contribution: Demonstrates LLM agents can guide opponents toward exploitable equilibria in competitive games and promote coordination in cooperative games, establishing opponent shaping as a key multi-agent dimension.

problem: Image understanding and synthesis typically require separate discriminative and generative approaches, missing opportunities for mutual reinforcement between perception and generation.
approach: GenRep jointly conducts discriminative learning and generative modeling by distilling diffusion model knowledge to guide perception, with gradient alignment strategy to reconcile both learning objectives.
contribution: Achieves top-leading performance on both image understanding and generation benchmarks through unified training that creates positive feedback loop between perception and synthesis tasks.

problem: Multimodal embedding models condense information into single vectors (limiting expressiveness) or produce too many vectors (expensive for retrieval), constraining practical scalability.
approach: MetaEmbed uses learnable Meta Tokens with Matryoshka Multi-Vector Retrieval training to learn information organization by granularity, enabling test-time scaling via token selection.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance scaling to 32B parameters with flexible test-time quality-efficiency tradeoffs on MMEB and ViDoRe benchmarks.

problem: LLM pre-training is expensive, requiring efficient data selection methods that balance quality estimates against coverage and diversity to optimize the Pareto frontier.
approach: Evaluates 22 data curation techniques on T5-style models, identifying AskLLM (using instruction-tuned LLM zero-shot assessment) and density sampling (modeling data distribution) as best methods.
contribution: Shows AskLLM consistently outperforms full-data training by 10% sampling and converges 70% faster, establishing data-efficient pre-training as viable alternative to full-dataset training.

problem: Tensor-based incomplete multi-view clustering requires expensive adjacency matrix post-processing and struggles to capture geometric graph structure with high computational complexity.
approach: CAMEL jointly learns view-specific embeddings with structured constraints and organizes them into tensors with low-rank constraints, approximating Laplacian degree with constant-degree matrices to reduce complexity.
contribution: Reduces computational complexity from O(n²) to O(1) while eliminating post-processing, achieving better clustering performance through coordinated optimization of graph connectivity and high-order correlations.

problem: Offline bandit evaluation using reward models remains vulnerable to adversarial manipulations that can drastically alter bandit behavior with imperceptible perturbations.
approach: Investigates adversarial robustness of offline bandits from linear to nonlinear (ReLU) reward functions, showing high-dimensional effects where perturbations become more effective as dimensionality increases.
contribution: Reveals striking vulnerability of high-dimensional offline bandits to adversarial attacks, establishing this as a key security concern for bandit-based evaluation of generative models.

problem: Text-to-image retrieval fails on short, underspecified queries that are semantically ambiguous and lack explicit quality control, limiting practical applicability.
approach: Uses generative LLM for quality-controllable query completion, conditioning enrichment on discretized quality levels derived from relevance and aesthetic scoring models.
contribution: Provides flexible, transparent, and controllable retrieval by extending underspecified queries into descriptive forms that capture visual attributes while enabling user-preferred quality steering.

problem: Credit assignment at arbitrary delays remains challenging, as standard exponentially decaying eligibility traces mix events during delays, complicating temporal precision in synaptic plasticity.
approach: Proposes cascading eligibility traces (CETs) formed by state-space models inspired by biochemical reaction cascades, providing temporally precise memory for delayed credit assignment.
contribution: Demonstrates CETs enable credit assignment at behavioral timescales from seconds to minutes and handle extremely slow retrograde signals, offering better basis for modeling synaptic plasticity.

problem: Existing peptide design approaches generate sequences and structures in decoupled manner, failing to ensure designs are physically stable, evolutionarily plausible, and internally coherent.
approach: PepTri uses SE(3)-equivariant diffusion framework jointly generating peptide sequences and 3D structures with three guidance signals: physics-informed, evolutionary, and mutual information.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on peptide-protein benchmarks with improved binding affinity, structural accuracy, and design diversity through tri-guided generative process.

problem: LLMs often express miscalibrated confidence in their answers, creating safety and trustworthiness concerns for their deployment in high-stakes applications.
approach: Uses reinforcement learning optimizing logarithmic scoring rule reward to fine-tune LLMs for expressing calibrated confidence estimates, directly penalizing both over- and under-confidence.
contribution: Shows models exhibit substantially improved calibration and generalize to unseen tasks, with emergent general confidence awareness from integrated calibration into generative process.

problem: Computing polar decomposition efficiently for GPU training differs sharply from classical settings, requiring algorithms prioritizing throughput over precision.
approach: Polar Express uses minimax optimization at each iteration to adapt update rules for matrix sign computation, maintaining efficiency with only matrix-matrix multiplications suitable for GPU deployment.
contribution: Converges rapidly both in early iterations and asymptotically, addresses finite-precision issues in bfloat16, and improves GPT-2 validation loss on FineWeb when integrated into Muon optimizer.

problem: Quantum error correction decoding faces fundamental accuracy-efficiency tradeoff between high-precision but expensive tensor networks and fast but less accurate neural methods.
approach: SAQ-Decoder combines transformer architecture with constraint-aware post-processing, using dual-stream architecture and differentiable logical loss to optimize logical error rates on finite fields.
contribution: Achieves near maximum likelihood accuracy (10.99% error threshold on toric codes vs 11.0% theoretical bound) with linear computational scalability, addressing key requirements for fault-tolerant quantum systems.

problem: LLM-based agents exhibit systematic latent source preferences that bias information selection toward particular publishers/platforms, potentially distorting information presentation to users.
approach: Conducts controlled experiments on twelve LLMs across news, research, and e-commerce tasks to identify and quantify latent source preferences encoded in parametric knowledge.
contribution: Shows several models consistently exhibit strong predictable source preferences sensitive to context, outweighing content influence, explaining phenomena like left-leaning news recommendation bias.

problem: Existing deep reinforcement learning workflow schedulers use rigid, single-path inference architectures that struggle with diverse scheduling scenarios and varying deadline requirements.
approach: DEFT introduces mixture-of-experts DRL architecture with specialized experts trained for different deadline tightness levels and graph-adaptive gating using cross-attention.
contribution: Significantly reduces execution cost and deadline violations across dynamic cloud workflow benchmarks, adaptively routing through appropriate experts for deadline-sensitive scheduling.

problem: Computer-use agents are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks, but current adversarial testing either lacks realism or ignores hybrid web-OS attack scenarios.
approach: RedTeamCUA introduces hybrid sandbox integrating VM-based OS with Docker-based web platforms, developing RTC-Bench with 864 examples for realistic adversarial scenario testing.
contribution: Benchmarks frontier CUAs showing Claude exhibits 42.9% Attack Success Rate while Operator shows 7.6%, revealing significant vulnerabilities even in most secure implementations.

problem: 3D object-scene composition with Gaussian Splatting suffers from baked appearance preventing realistic composition and requires expensive ray-tracing for relightable reconstruction.
approach: ComGS introduces Surface Octahedral Probes storing lighting/occlusion information for efficient querying via interpolation, and simplifies lighting by focusing on environment at object placement.
contribution: Achieves high-quality real-time rendering at ~26 FPS with at least 2× speedup in reconstruction, producing visually harmonious compositions through efficient inverse rendering.

problem: Brain-to-text decoding suffers from semantic mismatches during alignment, as human brains selectively encode salient regions based on individual interests not uniformly across scenes.
approach: Yo'Mind uses optimal transport-driven personalized semantic masking to adaptively mask redundant visual components based on individual neural responses, enabling unified brain-visual-linguistic alignment.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art brain-to-text reconstruction with improved interpretability and enables cross-subject decoding, bridging semantic gaps through personalized visual semantic pruning.

problem: Physics-informed neural networks suffer from spectral bias that causes networks to learn low-frequency features first, limiting accuracy on high-frequency PDEs.
approach: IFeF-PINN enriches latent space using high-frequency components through Random Fourier Features in iterative two-stage training: basis estimation then coefficient regression.
contribution: Empirically establishes Random Fourier Features enhance expressive capacity for high-frequency PDE approximation, showing superior performance over state-of-the-art on benchmark problems.

problem: SFT checkpoints with highest evaluation performance often fail to maximize RL potential due to distributional forgetting where models drift excessively from base model distribution.
approach: Identifies diversity metrics (entropy, self-BLEU) as reliable early-stopping criteria and introduces Adaptive Early-Stop Loss balancing new pattern acquisition with distribution preservation.
contribution: Shows diversity-based early stopping surpasses performance-based selection and AESL further enhances RL preparation on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Intermediate state in real-world processes often contains sparse activations whose identifiability and learnability through end-to-end training remains theoretically unestablished.
approach: Sparling proves Motif Identifiability Theorem establishing precise identification of sparse motifs through end-to-end error reduction, and provides algorithm using novel informational bottleneck enforcing extreme sparsity.
contribution: Precisely localizes intermediate states up to feature permutation with >90% accuracy on synthetic and real domains (DigitCircle, LaTeX-OCR, Audio-MNIST) through end-to-end training alone.
